sentences.text:
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 77/2024 dated 3.3.2024 registered at Police Station Harsud, District Khandwa for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366-A,
354, 376(2) (N) of the Indian Penal Code, Section 5L/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and Section 3(2)(v), 3(1)(w)(ii) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: It is contended that a perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. leaves no iota of doubt that the prosecutrix and the applicant were in relationship.
The prosecutrix went with the applicant on her own volition and there were consensual physical relations as well.
It is further submitted that at the time of incident the age of the prosecutrix was 17 years and 6 months and the age of the applicant was 23 years.
The applicant is in custody since 9.3.2024 and trial would take considerable time to conclude, therefore, the applicant be released on bail.
3. The counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that looking to the serious allegation against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

On perusal of case diary particularly the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it reflects that factum of relationship between the applicant and the prosecutrix is not disputed prima facie.
The applicant himself is aged about 23 years and is a first offender.

6. Thus, looking to the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 Cr.P.C., age of the applicant and the prosecutrix and period of custody of the applicant, this Court finds it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail.

Therefore,
without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant Sayyam Meena shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.

8. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
